name: Driving Over Stella
beta: Climb the steep slab beside the neighbouring arete, clipping five bolts before reaching a pair of anchors. The hardest moment is a lengthy stretch across a thin bulge.
overview: A good steep slab beside the Rebel Yell arete, with a big reach past a thin bulge for the crux.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Steep slab just right of the Rebel Yell arete

name: Drumstick Direct
beta:
Start to the right of a neighbouring route. Climb an easy flake, then trend leftward into the inner corner of an enormous cleft, and fight up the overhanging crack above with strenuous fist jams to a ledge higher and to the right.

The second pitch trends rightward into an easier corner. Rack mostly medium wired nuts and plenty of cams up to four inches.
overview: A crack that takes hand and fist jams, rated among the better lines on its rock. The overhanging crack on the first pitch is the hard part; the second pitch is far easier.

current.area_walk_in: From the end of the road, a short trail climbs to the saddle between Turkey Rock and the Turkey Perch. Turkey Tail is the buttress off to the north (left) of the Perch, reached by crossing a talus field.
current.descent: rappel with double ropes after the first pitch
current.location: starts to the east, beside For Turkeys Only

name: Dumb Waiter
beta: Clip the bolts up the face to the right of the chimney, finishing at the lowering anchors.
overview: A fun bolted route up the west side of a pillar located right of a neighbouring wall.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the trail from the lot, staying straight at the signed turn for the Far Side. At the next signed junction take the left fork toward the prow, cross the wash, and climb switchbacks up the steep slope to the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on the west side of the pillar, just to the right of the chimney

name: Earth Voyage
beta: On pitch one, climb as far as the first bolt of the neighbouring route, then veer left under the bulges, where the crux sits, reach a hand crack, and angle up rightward to a belay on slings beside a band of roofs. Pitch two crosses the roof band toward the left, then works rightward across a slab.
overview: A route on a very steep wall beside a neighbouring line, with the hardest moves low down. The first lead can be bypassed by using the neighbour's opening pitch.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the obvious trail south from the lot, then drop around the formation through a notch and down a gully. If the ground begins to feel like fifth class, you have gone too far.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: very steep wall directly west of China Doll

name: El Camino Real
beta:
Start up the huge neighbouring dihedral route, then bridge outward toward the right to arrive at the foot of a slender crack in the dihedral's right wall. Constant finger jams and laybacks lead to a tiny perch with a pair of shuts; the crux comes about midway up the crack.

From there, rappel or press on past an old knifeblade to link with another route.
overview: One of the hardest free climbs on Lumpy Ridge: relentless finger jamming and laybacking up a thin seam high on the Book's great dihedral, its right-hand face.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, hike west past the Twin Owls formation and follow the Black Canyon Trail to The Book, adding roughly another two-thirds of a mile beyond Twin Owls. Scramble up to the base of the Pages Wall.
current.descent: Rappel from the cold shuts; with one rope, expect about 15 ft of downclimbing
current.anchor: two cold shuts on a small stance

name: Safari Land
beta: It shares a start with Trunk Line, but above the roof you shift right to reach a bolt.
overview: Begins on the Trunk Line start, then steps right over the roof to reach a bolt.

current.descent: rappel from the cabled anchors at the summit's east end
current.location: Starts where Trunk Line does, at the southeast corner

name: End of an Era
beta: Airy face moves follow a sharp, attractive bolted edge to the right of a neighbouring route, up to lowering anchors about 70 feet off the ground. A second pitch carries on up and leftward over easier ground.
overview: Exposed climbing on a sharp, bolted arete to a lower-off about 70 ft up; an easier second pitch wanders up and left.

current.area_walk_in: Walk uphill on the established trails toward the face; the long dihedral on the face makes an easy landmark to aim for.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: lowering station about 70 ft up (top of pitch 1)
current.location: on the sharp bolted arete immediately right of New Era's big corner

name: Facial Hair
beta: Start right of a neighbouring route, get up onto a flake and sling it for gear. A short crack leads to a mantle, then three bolts take you up the face, finishing in an easier corner.
overview: A slung flake and short leaning crack to mantles, then three bolts of thin face and an easy corner finish.

current.descent: descend the 4th-class groove at the rock’s left edge
current.location: Just around the corner right of Gollum’s Arch, starting at a flake you sling for pro

name: Building Bottrell
beta: Follow the leaning edge at the face's southern extreme, beside the big fir. Hardest is the third clip, and four cold shuts lead to paired chains.
overview: Tracks the tilted edge at the southern limit of the wall, beside the big fir. Getting past the third bolt is the stiffest moment.

current.area_walk_in: A brief, steep, eroded track fords the creek and ascends the slope to the wall's foot. Numbering runs north to south; to find route one, start at the Buoux Block and head north.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Southern end of the wall, beside the big fir tree

name: Fascist Drill in the West
beta: Work up into the leftward-facing dihedral, sharing the start of its harder neighbour, then at the roof pull out right and follow the line of bolts up the face. Long runners help with the early clips. The belay is a slanting shelf where slings are needed.
overview: Excellent bolted face on the Book: up a short corner, right round the roof, then sustained slab and face climbing on bolts.

current.descent: Single-rope rappel, which needs about 15 ft of downclimbing

rack_items.sizes: long slings kept for early clips

name: Fast Draw
beta:
The first lead takes the obvious crack that starts as fingers and widens to hands, up the face's right flank. Thin finger jams past a few old bolts are the crux; mid-size cams protect the hands section.

Near its end, a piton-protected face traverse heads left into a second crack, which squeezes awkwardly to a bolted belay ledge. Going straight up that upper crack is an alternative to the traverse.
overview: Two-pitch Kor classic to a tiny, exposed summit: fingers to hands up the north side, then an offwidth-chimney finish.

current.descent: rap 70 ft to the ledge, then 140 ft to the ground

name: Fields of Dreams Growing Wild
beta: Mostly bolt-protected friction up the central buttress of this big slab, with the runouts coming higher up on the easier-angled ground.
overview: A Big Rock classic: a long, chiefly bolted friction line up the central buttress, with sparser protection on the easier ground near the top.

current.location: takes the central buttress of the dome

name: Final Exam
beta: Fingertip laybacks up a short, steep bulge beside the big overhang make the whole problem. Above it, slabs continue: finish through the roof, cross rightward into the neighbouring crack system, or descend the slabs on the left by downclimbing.
overview: A short, bouldery classic on Castle Rock's western flank: a steep bulge climbed on fingertip liebacks, then easy slabs above with options to continue or scramble off.

current.area_walk_in: The base of the formation is a short flat step from the roadside pullout; the ground at the foot is uneven.
current.descent: scramble back down the leftward slabs, or keep going higher
current.location: Castle Rock's west flank, beside (left of) a big overhang, with Coffin Crack's wide slot next door on the right

name: Finger Lickin' Good
beta: Begin on a thin crack slanting rightward, where the opening moves of dicey face climbing are the hardest. Stop on a little perch under the finger crack; splitting the route in two keeps rope drag down. Jam the crack to a flake belay, then rappel. Bring small gear.
overview: A rightward thin crack with tricky face moves leads to a superb straight-in finger crack; usually split in two to cut rope drag.

current.descent: rap 80 ft to the ground
current.location: A thin crack some 30 ft to the right of the Pressure Drop start

name: Finger  Tripping
beta: Start lower and farther left than a neighbouring dihedral route. Climb a smooth slab clipping three newer bolts to the shared belay, then carry on over another slab with one more bolt, right of that dihedral, to gain the ledge used for walking off.
overview: Bolted slab friction to the Magical Chrome belay, then a second slab beside that route’s corner.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: walk off left from the ledge after two pitches
current.location: Down and left of the Magical Chrome start, just left of the little buttress

name: Flash Dihedral (Knapp Version)
beta: The line is the shallow dihedral in the northwest face, started from a broken pile of blocks. Bring long slings.
overview: Short line up a shallow corner on the northwest side of the First Buttress, often set up as a toprope.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: From a broken pile of rock roughly 50 ft higher than the steel pipe

name: Flat Earth Society
beta: Edge up the thin slab past two bolts, then take the crack that angles left, hand-traversing leftward along it. Thin face moves back right past two more bolts lead to the anchors; veering right at the last bolt gives an easier finish.
overview: Thin slab edging leads to a crack slanting left, a hand traverse, then delicate face moves to cold shuts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Just left of the big dihedral that faces left

name: Flight for Life
beta: Begin from the ledge halfway up the face, at its left side. Climb a handful of bolts, heading left initially and then right as you near the overhang. Pull over the lip, clip one last bolt, then finish up to the anchors; a rappel returns you to the ground.
overview: A sustained bolted face below the arch’s left end, finishing over the roof to a bolt anchor.

current.descent: rap 80 ft, or add a 5.10a face pitch to the top
current.location: Left end of the mid-height ledge on the lower wall; scramble broken ground below and right to reach it

name: Forrest Solo
beta: Approach the spire from its north side, then climb two rope-lengths of steep, overhanging rock up the west face.
overview: A two-pitch line up the steep, overhanging west flank of the small pinnacle at the foot of the buttress; first done as an aid solo and later freed.

current.area_walk_in: One option is to follow the Deer Mountain summit trail to its northernmost switchback, level with the lowest part of the cliff, then step off the path and traverse eastward to the cliff's foot. The alternative is a direct, steep slog up the hillside, about 1,400 vertical feet.
current.location: On the overhanging west side of the Praying Nun pinnacle, reached by coming in from the north

name: Get A Life
beta:
The first lead goes up a loose groove into the dihedral, stemming and jamming to a two-inch crack and a niche belay. The second works the same dihedral to a roomy ledge with bolts.

The crux is a short, strenuous, overhanging finger crack in the corner above that ledge. After that, jam a crack along an arete, traverse right beneath a big roof, then face climb leftward past bolts toward a drilled pin and steady face moves to the anchors.
overview: A demanding five-pitch crack line on the south side of a pillar. A loose chimney and groove leads into a corner, and the third pitch, a thin finger crack that overhangs, is the crux.

current.descent: three double-rope rappels down the line
current.location: Obvious crack line on the pillar's south face, visible up and left once the trail has switchbacked through the cliff band

name: Give the Dog a Bone
beta: Follow an arching corner past a pair of bolts. Where the corner curves to the right, break out left over the roof and carry on up steep terrain, ending at a shelf with a two-bolt anchor.
overview: Steep bolted line that leaves a curving 5.10 corner, pulls a roof leftward and finishes up a sustained headwall to a ledge.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares the opening corner with Coney Island Baby, then branches left onto the headwall about 25 ft up

name: Good Timing
beta:
Tackle the slab and overhang just as a neighbouring route does, then shift left along a ledge to a belay of two bolts.

Head up and a touch left past the bolts, which hold the crux, to reach a crack and a good stance; a final crack lead goes to a tree.
overview: Fine slab and edging: the Trippage start, a bolted second pitch, then a crack to a tree.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: head up rightward and descend the eastern crest until a ramp leads into the forest
current.location: Share the Trippage opening (slab, then roof), then step left to a bolted stance

name: Grey Rat Rocksicle
beta: Start from high on the ramp and work left into a flared slot, then step out right and climb corners and disconnected cracks toward the roof's right side. Bring small gear and be ready to improvise placements.
overview: A route that links corners and broken cracks toward the right-hand end of a huge roof, finishing at a ledge over it.

current.descent: walk off southwest down the ramps
current.location: upper section of the ramp

name: Heaven Can Wait
beta: Jam cracks up the corner that faces left to the tree standing on a roomy shelf, from which a walk-off heads right. An optional second pitch climbs easy rock leftward beneath the arch before retracing the same moves back to the ledge.
overview: Cracks in a corner facing left lead to a tree-topped big ledge, with an optional runout extension toward the arch.

current.descent: walk off right along the big ledge
current.location: Corner facing left, below the main arch’s left end

name: Heavenly Journey
beta:
The line blazes over the featureless slab left of the Right Dihedral. The first pitch is a finger crack curving like a sickle, ending at a belay of two bolts.

The second, a friction pitch, angles leftward with little to clip until the final belay.
overview: A famous bold slab: a curved finger crack up to a bolted stance, then a long, nearly unprotected friction pitch.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: one-rope rap of about 75 ft north from the summit bolts, or downclimb west then north (easy)
current.location: Smooth slab west of the Right Dihedral corner, starting up a curved, sickle-like finger crack

name: Hollow Flake
beta: A big flake rests against the face. Ascend the middle of it, or along its right edge, to a ledge with a tree, then rappel to the ground.
overview: Climb the middle or right edge of a big leaning flake to a tree-ledge belay and rappel off.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.
current.descent: rap from the tree ledge
current.location: On the big flake propped against the cliff, right of the Staircase line

name: Hot Licks
beta: Start up the neighbouring Great Dihedral, then peel off leftward onto a hand-sized crack a short way above the ground. Follow that crack for about a rope-length, stopping wherever is comfortable. Expect an offwidth section and bring plenty of big cams.
overview: Three pitches that open with a hand crack beside the Great Dihedral and finish with a sustained, exposed offwidth.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Lumpy Ridge trail west past the old Twin Owls area, continue beyond the Book and the Bookmark, then take a faint spur to the southeast prow. A little scrambling is needed to get to the routes on the right.
current.location: Begin in the Great Dihedral and step left almost immediately into a wide hand crack

name: Hot Rize
beta: Clip a series of bolts to gain the rounded arete, then keep climbing upward along it.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the arete on the dome's southeast face, taking its right-hand side

name: Hurricane Gloria
beta:
Begin beside an enormous flake and follow the line of bolts to the steep headwall, where the moves reach 5.12. The two-bolt hanging stance sits within the crux section, so it works as a rest.

From the stance, trend up and left onto a crack that ends the route. Take gear up to about three inches.
overview: A good bolt-protected face route tracing a dark streak up the steep middle slab. It can be split into two pitches or run as a single full-rope pitch to the top slabs.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: lower or rappel at the first stance chains, or carry on to the upper slabs
current.location: starts beside the giant flake, then follows a dark stain up the middle slab

name: Iron Cross
beta: A dihedral that zigs right, left and right again passes a pin and ends at a belay on a pair of ring bolts; from there the route moves left and follows bolts.
overview: A zigzagging dihedral that flips left, right, then left again, with a fixed pin along it. It ends at a belay on two ring bolts, and the line goes on from there up a bolt-protected stretch.

current.area_walk_in: The ridge base sits in the woods just above the huge Superfresh boulder, a couple of hundred yards beyond the tight mouth of Fern Canyon.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Ivory Coast
beta: Work a grubby crack that angles rightward up into the east-side corner, then fight through the roof with hard jamming. Bring mid-size to big protection.
overview: A right-slanting crack in a corner on Elephant Rock's east face, ending with hard jams through a strange roof.

current.descent: rap off the cabled anchors at the summit's east end
current.location: Eastern side of the rock, in a dirty crack that angles right up a corner to an odd roof

name: J-Crack
beta:
First pitch: friction rightward off the start of a neighbouring route to reach a groove under the crack, finishing via a short slot to a belay on the narrowing ledge.

Second pitch: make a bold foot-shuffle leftward into the foot of the J, then jam flawless finger-width crack for roughly 140 feet to a cramped pod. A harder alternate start uses a bolt and a piton.
overview: One of the most popular climbs on Lumpy Ridge: sidestep leftward on footholds to where a J-shaped crack starts, then a long stretch of superb finger jamming.

current.descent: Usual way down heads east over slabs, then south through deadfall; a brief third-class step lands above the Cave, then an eastward channel leads onto an airy ledge holding two big pines, then down a third-class gully that is frequently wet

name: Jackpot
beta: Climb the dark groove, then pull onto devious overhanging rock using good holds before some tricky moves higher up. Fourteen bolts keep it well protected.
overview: A long bolted line that follows a dark groove into steep, overhanging rock, with good holds through the steepness and a puzzling sequence near the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts at the bottom of the dark groove that the line follows

name: Face the Face
beta: Start by a big tree right of the west-leaning ramp. Steep face past three bolts, then easier ground and two more bolts lead to the anchors.
overview: Steep face climbing opens the route, then easier rock continues to the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: start by a big tree, just beyond the notch and a little right of a ramp system that leans west

name: Lego Land
beta: Start from boulders and follow a water streak across the central slab; protection is sparse low down, so expect a runout on easier ground. Five bolts guard the steeper top section, which has a little friction climbing near the finish.
overview: Climbs a water streak past two bolts, then thins out its protection on easier ground before a steeper, well-bolted upper slab.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts on the boulders at the central slab

name: Mythical Kings and Iguanas
beta: Scamper up easy ground from the gully, then weave through a series of overlaps in the steep centre of the slab. Five bolts; small wired nuts can add protection.
overview: Fine climbing up the steepest part of the slab: easy ground first, then a weave through several overlaps.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the steep center of the slab, reached up the access gully

name: Nervous Disorder
beta: Smooth, steep slab beside a blunt arete, protected by seven bolts, steepens into a headwall below the anchors.
overview: Steep smooth slab climbing on the left flank of a blunt tilted arete, then a steeper headwall under the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: far west edge of the southwest side, beside large boulders under a gravel-filled gully

name: Tease
beta: Scramble the ramp in the gully to a belay on top of a boulder. Start at the cold shut, then three further bolts carry you up the easier-angled slab to the anchors.
overview: A good, moderate single pitch that starts from the boulder-top stance and finishes on the gentler slab above.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: reach the boulder-top stance via the ramps of the east-side gully

name: Javelin
beta: A strenuous overhanging crack taken with a mix of finger-sized and hand-sized jams, right of its neighbour Cello. Finish at the fixed anchors or traverse off left to a tree.
overview: A strenuous 1978 classic: jam fingers and hands up a steep, overhanging crack just to the right of Cello, ending at fixed anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Find the climbers' trail through the forest and up the steep talus slope, heading for the canyon just right of the main wall. Loose rock is common, so avoid kicking stones down onto others.
current.descent: rappel from the fixed anchors, or continue leftward to belay at a tree
current.anchor: fixed anchors at the top of the crack
current.location: The pronounced overhanging crack just right of Cello

name: Jazzman (a.k.a. Turdland)
beta: Go to the first bolt of the neighbouring Birdland, then face-climb beside a blunt edge on its left. Pack big nuts plus small cams for protection.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: follow the neighbouring line to its first bolt, then veer left past a blunt edge
